title: Licensing, documents and new drivers
summary: What licence categories exist, how you get a licence, what applies to a new driver, which documents are mandatory — and when medical fitness decides.

lessons.title: Licence categories and minimum ages
lessons.summary: Every licence category is defined by the type of vehicle, its weight and its number of passengers — not by a general name.
lessons.body:
"Licence for a private car" and "licence for a truck" are convenient labels, but in law every [[term:license-category|licence category]] is defined precisely: which vehicle, up to what weight, with how many passengers.

# The main categories
| Category | Allows driving a — |
|---|---|
| [[term:license-category-b|B]] | Motor vehicle up to {{fact:licence.b.max_weight}}, up to {{fact:licence.b.max_passengers}} passengers besides the driver (not including a taxi, tour vehicle or public bus) |
| A2 | Motorcycle up to {{fact:licence.a2.max_cc}} cc and up to {{fact:licence.a2.max_kw}} |
| A1 | Motorcycle up to {{fact:licence.a1.max_kw}} |
| [[term:license-category-a|A]] | Motorcycle of any power |
| 1 | Tractor, mobile machine, forklift up to {{fact:licence.tractor.forklift_max}}, ATV (with a permit), off-road vehicle |
| C1 | Commercial vehicle and work vehicle {{fact:licence.c1.weight_range}} |
| [[term:license-category-c|C]] | Commercial vehicle and work vehicle over {{fact:licence.c.min_weight}} |
| C+E | A vehicle as in C, also with a trailer or supported trailer |
| D1 | Taxi, tour vehicle, minibus |
| D2 / D3 | Minibus up to {{fact:licence.d2.max_passengers}} passengers |
| [[term:license-category-d|D]] | Bus of any size |

Each row is a separate regulation in the Traffic Regulations (176 to 185) — so a B licence, for example, also allows driving an ATV, a mobile machine (except a forklift) and an off-road vehicle, not only a "private car" in the everyday sense.

# Minimum age
| Category | Minimum age |
|---|---|
| A2, theory test for all categories | {{fact:theory.min_age}} (for the theory test) |
| B | {{fact:licence.b.min_age}} (learning from age {{fact:licence.b.learning_age}}) |
| A1 | {{fact:licence.a1.min_age}} |
| A2 | {{fact:licence.a2.min_age}} |
| A | {{fact:licence.a.min_age}}, and with {{fact:licence.a.seniority_a1}} of seniority in A1 |
| 1 (tractor) | {{fact:licence.tractor.min_age}} |
| C1 | {{fact:licence.c1.min_age}} |
| C | {{fact:licence.c.min_age}}, and with {{fact:licence.c.seniority_c1}} of seniority in C1 |
| C+E | {{fact:licence.ce.min_age}}, and with {{fact:licence.ce.seniority_c}} of seniority in C |
| D1, D2 | {{fact:licence.d1.min_age}} (D1), {{fact:licence.d2.min_age}} (D2) — both require {{fact:licence.d1.seniority_b}} of seniority in B or C1 |
| D | {{fact:licence.d.min_age}}, and with {{fact:licence.d1.seniority_b}} of seniority in B or C1 |

:::remember
Most of the "higher" categories — C, C+E, D — require not only age but also **seniority** in the previous category. You cannot jump straight to a heavy truck or bus licence.
:::

# A B-licence holder is exempt from some things
Someone who already holds a [[term:license-category-b|B licence]] is exempt from the theory test when applying for a motorcycle licence, and after {{fact:licence.a.seniority_a1}} years of seniority in B — is also exempt from the road-behaviour test for an A2/A1 licence. A mobility scooter and an ATV with the appropriate permit also do not require a separate licence category in every case — details in the [[chapter:road-basics|The road and its users]] chapter.
keyPoints: Every licence category is defined by the type of vehicle, its weight and its number of passengers — not by a general name.
A B licence has both a learning age ({{fact:licence.b.learning_age}}) and a licence age ({{fact:licence.b.min_age}}) — different from each other.
Categories C, C+E, D and D2/D3 require seniority in a lower category, not just age.
A B-licence holder is exempt from the theory test for a motorcycle, and after the required seniority — also from the road-behaviour test.

lessons.title: The road to a licence: from theory to the practical test
lessons.summary: Eye test, theory exam, driving lessons and the practical test — the order it happens in, and the rules of each stage.
lessons.body:
For a B licence, for example, there are three separate stages — in a particular order.

# Stage 1: eye test and medical declaration
Before anything else, the applicant fills in a digital declaration about their medical condition and undergoes an [[term:eye-exam|eye test]] on a device approved by the Ministry of Health (reg. 192(b)). If the declaration is clear — they are cleared to continue; if a concern arises, they are referred to an authorised doctor (see the [[chapter:licensing|Licensing, documents and new drivers]] chapter, the "Medical fitness" lesson later on).

# Stage 2: the theory exam
:::law
You can sit the [[term:theory-test|theory exam]] from age {{fact:theory.min_age}}, even before starting actual driving lessons.
:::

The exam has {{fact:theory.questions}} questions on {{fact:theory.topics}} topics: traffic law, signs, correct behaviour on the road, and vehicle knowledge. The exam lasts {{fact:theory.time_limit}}, and you pass it with at least {{fact:theory.pass_correct}} correct answers — meaning up to {{fact:theory.max_mistakes}} mistakes allowed. Failed? The licensing authority may set a date for a retest, no later than {{fact:theory.retest_max_wait}} from the day of the exam you failed.

:::remember
Exam and test results are valid for {{fact:theory.validity}} only. Anyone who has not finished all the stages within this time will have to be tested again.
:::

# Stage 3: driving lessons and the practical test
For a B licence you can start learning to drive in practice from age {{fact:licence.b.learning_age}}, with a qualified [[term:driving-instructor|driving instructor]], usually through a [[term:driving-school|driving school]] — a minimum of {{fact:licence.b.min_lessons}} [[term:driving-lesson|driving lessons]]. At the end of training, you take the [[term:practical-test|practical test]] with a [[term:driving-examiner|driving test examiner]] appointed by the licensing authority — a test of actual driving, on urban and non-urban roads, that checks both technical control and safe decision-making.

# And then — the licence
Anyone who has passed all the stages and has turned {{fact:licence.b.min_age}} receives the licence. If they are a "young [[term:new-driver|new driver]]" (under {{fact:newdriver.young.age}}) — the first licence is a temporary provisional licence, and the escort programme applies to them. Full details in the next lesson.

:::tip
You can sit the theory exam early, even before the learning age — so that by the time you reach the learning age, you can already focus on the driving itself.
:::
keyPoints: Order of stages: medical declaration and eye test ← theory exam (from age {{fact:theory.min_age}}) ← driving lessons (at least {{fact:licence.b.min_lessons}}) ← practical test.
The theory exam has {{fact:theory.questions}} questions on {{fact:theory.topics}} topics; you pass with {{fact:theory.pass_correct}} correct answers ({{fact:theory.max_mistakes}} mistakes at most).
Exam results are valid for {{fact:theory.validity}} only.
A B licence is issued only from age {{fact:licence.b.min_age}}, even if all stages were completed earlier.

lessons.title: New driver: the escort period and restrictions
lessons.summary: {{fact:newdriver.duration}} with special rules, and an escort programme of {{fact:newdriver.escort.hours_total}} for a young new driver — why, and how it works.
lessons.body:
New drivers are involved in accidents at a higher rate than experienced drivers — not from lack of knowledge, but from lack of experience in judging danger and reacting quickly. That is why the law places temporary restrictions on a [[term:new-driver|new driver]].

# Who is a new driver, and for how long
The [[term:probation-period|new-driver period]] lasts {{fact:newdriver.duration}} from the day the first licence is received, and a conviction for an offence under the Third Schedule to the Ordinance extends it by a further {{fact:newdriver.extension}}. A "young new driver" is a new driver who has not yet turned {{fact:newdriver.young.age}} — and the strictest restrictions apply to them.

# The escort programme
:::law
A young new driver shall drive with an [[term:accompanying-driver|accompanying driver]] for at least {{fact:newdriver.escort.hours_total}}: {{fact:newdriver.escort.hours_urban}} on urban roads, {{fact:newdriver.escort.hours_nonurban}} on non-urban roads, and {{fact:newdriver.escort.hours_night}} at night (reg. 175B).
:::

The first licence is a temporary [[term:provisional-license|provisional licence]], valid for {{fact:newdriver.permit_validity}}. Full escort (at any hour of the day) lasts {{fact:newdriver.escort.day_months}} from the day the licence is received, followed by another {{fact:newdriver.escort.night_months}} of escort at night hours only ({{fact:newdriver.escort.night_hours}}).

An accompanying driver must meet a minimum age and seniority: {{fact:newdriver.escort.companion_age_a}} and {{fact:newdriver.escort.companion_years_a}} of seniority (track A), or {{fact:newdriver.escort.companion_age_b}} and {{fact:newdriver.escort.companion_years_b}} of seniority (track B). Someone eligible for state funding can complete {{fact:newdriver.escort.hours_funded}} of the hours with a qualified driving instructor instead of a private accompanying driver.

:::remember
Someone who has completed the IDF's driver mentoring programme is [[term:accompanying-driver|exempt]] from the escort programme (reg. 175D).
:::

# Further restrictions
- **Passengers**: up to age {{fact:newdriver.passengers.age}}, a new driver may carry no more than {{fact:newdriver.passengers.max}} passengers without an accompanying driver, even after the escort period.
- **The "[[term:new-driver-label|new driver]]" label**: mandatory on the rear window, on a vehicle whose gross vehicle weight is up to {{fact:newdriver.sign.weight_limit}}.
- **Alcohol**: a new driver is subject to the stricter alcohol threshold — {{fact:alcohol.strict.breath}} in breath — for the whole new-driver period (see the [[chapter:human-factor|The driver: the human factor]] chapter).

:::fine
A young new driver driving without an accompanying driver, or with more passengers than allowed without one, is an offence tried in court. Details in the [[chapter:enforcement|Offences, fines and points]] chapter.
:::
keyPoints: New-driver period: {{fact:newdriver.duration}}; a young new driver is under {{fact:newdriver.young.age}}.
Escort programme: {{fact:newdriver.escort.hours_total}} — {{fact:newdriver.escort.hours_urban}} urban, {{fact:newdriver.escort.hours_nonurban}} non-urban, {{fact:newdriver.escort.hours_night}} night.
Up to age {{fact:newdriver.passengers.age}} — no more than {{fact:newdriver.passengers.max}} passengers without an accompanying driver.
The stricter alcohol threshold applies to a new driver for the whole period.

lessons.title: The documents that must be valid
lessons.summary: Driving licence, vehicle licence, compulsory insurance and the periodic test — what each one is, and what happens when it expires.
lessons.body:
Four documents must be valid on every journey — for the vehicle and the driver alike. If even one of them has expired, even if the vehicle is roadworthy and the driver careful, that is an offence.

# The driving licence
A [[term:driving-license|driving licence]] for the regular categories (B and above) is usually issued for a period of up to {{fact:licence.validity_years}} (reg. 173), but a [[term:new-driver|new driver]] first receives a much shorter permit, and anyone due for repeat medical checks (from age {{fact:licence.medical.pro_from_age|n}} for categories C and above, and from age {{fact:licence.medical.b_first_age|n}} for other licences, such as B) renews it according to that schedule (see the "Medical fitness" lesson later on). [[term:license-renewal|Renewing the licence]] requires paying a fee, and sometimes also a repeat [[term:eye-exam|eye test]].

:::fine
Driving with an expired driving licence — a fine and points if it expired recently; the longer the time that has passed, the harsher the penalty, up to an offence tried in court. Details in the [[chapter:enforcement|Offences, fines and points]] chapter.
:::

# The vehicle licence
A [[term:vehicle-license|vehicle licence]] shows that the vehicle is registered, that it has passed the [[term:vehicle-annual-test|periodic test]] ("the test") when required, and that the fee has been paid. It is valid for {{fact:vehiclelicence.validity}} generally, and for a tractor — {{fact:vehiclelicence.validity_tractor}}.

# The periodic test ("the test")
A new private vehicle (registered from 1 January 2023) undergoes its first periodic test {{fact:vehicletest.private.first_test_years}} from the date of registration, and afterwards once every {{fact:vehicletest.private.interval_years}}. The test examines brakes, steering, lights, emissions, the chassis and the wheels — all dependent on the vehicle being in a condition that does not endanger road users (reg. 27).

# Compulsory insurance
:::law
No person shall drive a motor vehicle without a valid [[term:compulsory-insurance|compulsory insurance policy]] (Motor Vehicle Insurance Ordinance). This is insurance that covers bodily injury to passengers and pedestrians who are hurt — regardless of fault.
:::

:::fine
Driving without valid compulsory insurance is an offence tried in court, and can lead to a licence disqualification of at least {{fact:insurance.no_insurance.min_disqualification}}.
:::

# What must be in the vehicle
Besides the documents — a warning triangle, a reflective vest and a working spare wheel (in a vehicle with a kerb weight over {{fact:equip.spare_wheel}}) are mandatory equipment that must be in a motor vehicle (except a motorcycle), even though you are not always required to show them.

# Transferring ownership
When you sell a vehicle, you must update the licensing authority about the change of ownership — otherwise the registered owner may be held responsible for offences committed by the new owner.
keyPoints: Four documents valid on every journey: driving licence, vehicle licence, compulsory insurance, and a periodic test when required.
A new private vehicle is first tested after {{fact:vehicletest.private.first_test_years}}, and then every {{fact:vehicletest.private.interval_years}}.
Driving without valid compulsory insurance can lead to a licence disqualification of at least {{fact:insurance.no_insurance.min_disqualification}}.
Mandatory equipment — triangle, vest and spare wheel — must actually be in the vehicle, not just purchased once.

lessons.title: Medical fitness to drive
lessons.summary: Vision, hearing and general health — the licence depends on ongoing fitness, not just a one-time test.
lessons.body:
A driving licence is not a certificate you get once and forget about. Medical fitness is an ongoing condition — and you must also report when it changes.

# When applying for a licence
Every licence applicant fills in a digital declaration about their medical condition and undergoes an [[term:eye-exam|eye test]] on a device approved by the Ministry of Health (reg. 192(b)). If a need is found, they are referred for examination by an **authorised doctor**, who may issue a [[term:medical-certificate|medical certificate for driving]] with conditions: for example, a requirement to wear glasses or contact lenses, noted on the driving licence itself (reg. 194).

For licences D1 through D (taxi, bus) and for special permits, a minimum hearing fitness is also required — at least {{fact:licence.medical.hearing_db}} in one ear (reg. 197).

:::fine
Driving without the optical aid (glasses or lenses) the licence requires — a fine offence, even if your vision is actually fine at that moment.
:::

# When your health changes
:::law
A licence holder in whom heart disease, or changes in the nervous system, bones, vision or hearing are discovered, shall report this **immediately** by registered letter to the licensing authority (reg. 13).
:::

This is not a recommendation — it is a legal duty. If someone submits false or misleading information in the medical declaration, or fails to report a change as required, the licensing authority may refuse to issue them a licence, suspend it, or not renew it.

# Repeat checks with age
Even someone with no required change must undergo repeat checks from a certain age: a holder of a licence for categories C and above (C1, C, C+E, D1–D) and a qualified instructor — once every {{fact:licence.medical.pro_every_years}} from age {{fact:licence.medical.pro_from_age|n}} to age {{fact:licence.medical.pro_frequent_from_age|n}}, and from age {{fact:licence.medical.pro_frequent_from_age|n}} — once every {{fact:licence.medical.frequent_every_years}}. A holder of a B licence only — at age {{fact:licence.medical.b_first_age|n}} and at age {{fact:licence.medical.b_second_age|n}}, and after that once every {{fact:licence.medical.frequent_every_years}} (reg. 196).

:::remember
Anyone who does not attend the required check, or is examined and found unfit — their licence **will not be renewed**.
:::

# Disputing the decision
Anyone who feels wronged by the authorised doctor's decision may appeal to an appeals committee within {{fact:licence.medical.appeal_days}} of the day the decision was given to them (reg. 195). The appeals committee can confirm, change or cancel the decision, or order a repeat examination.

:::tip
A new medication that affects alertness, eye surgery, or a new medical diagnosis — all of these may require an update to the licensing authority. When you are not sure, it is best to check with your family doctor.
:::
keyPoints: An eye test and a medical declaration are conditions for getting a licence; the authorised doctor may set conditions such as a requirement to wear glasses.
A significant change in health (heart, nerves, vision, hearing) must be reported to the licensing authority immediately (reg. 13).

Repeat medical checks apply by age and by licence category — usually every {{fact:licence.medical.frequent_every_years}} after age {{fact:licence.medical.pro_frequent_from_age|n}}/{{fact:licence.medical.b_second_age|n}}.
You can appeal the authorised doctor's decision to an appeals committee within {{fact:licence.medical.appeal_days}}.
